ptt_rules: kind must be 'button' (momentary); never an encoder turn, a rotary-switch pulse, a funky turn or a gear paddle
its signal on the platform must be unique (not folded with another control) and not 'none'
prefer reach 'thumb'; never a control already holding a time-critical action (DRS, overtake)
F1 25: bound in the game as UDP Action N (N = the layout's ptt action, default 1)
games without button telemetry: no wheel control; Pitwall push-to-talk is the iPad's talk button or Space on a keyboard

fixed_by_game.text: GT7 sets this coloured stick itself: Pitwall can't change it. Which colour does what is community-reported.

not_possible.text: No game Pitwall knows lets you change ride height while driving. F1 25 and GT7 only show it in the car setup; iRacing's weight jacker on some oval cars is the closest thing.

In most games researched, wing angles are set in the car setup, not while driving. iRacing lists front and rear wing buttons for cars that have them (community, unverified). F1 25's 2026 cars switch Active Aero to Straight Line Mode with the DRS/S Mode button, inside the zones only; other games have DRS on cars that have it.
GT7's stability control (ASM) and ABS are only in the pause menu, under Assistance Settings. They can't go on a button.
In F1 25, traction control and ABS are assists you set in the menu, not while driving.
{game} doesn't send wheel button presses, so Pitwall can't see your wheel. Talk to Pitwall with the iPad's talk button, or hold Space on a keyboard.

Pitwall can show the current value only where the game sends it: F1 25 brake bias and ERS mode. GT7 only says when TCS is working, not its level; Assetto Corsa on console only says whether TC and ABS are on and working.

steps: Open the game's Controls (sometimes Controller, Wheel or Bindings) menu.
Pick your wheel or its preset if the game lists one.
For each row on Pitwall's card, find the game's action with that meaning (the names it may use are listed) and press the control on your wheel.
Save, then check each one on track. Pitwall can't see your wheel in this game.

reasons.pair:encoder: {fn} on {ctl}: you change it during a race, and turning one encoder gives + and − under your thumb.
reasons.pair:encoder_far: {fn} on {ctl}: you change it during a race, and turning one encoder gives + and −.
reasons.pair:rocker: {fn} on {ctl}: one rocker, up for +, down for −.
reasons.pair:dpad: {fn} on {ctl} ({a} for +, {b} for −): opposite directions of one control are easy to find by feel.
reasons.pair:buttons_same_zone: {fn}: + on {a_ctl} and − on {b_ctl}, two buttons side by side.
reasons.pair:buttons: {fn}: + on {a_ctl} and − on {b_ctl}, the best free buttons left.
reasons.ptt:f1: Talk to Pitwall on {ctl}: a plain button you can hold with your thumb. Map it to UDP Action {n} in F1 25 so Pitwall sees it.
reasons.hold:thumb: {fn} on {ctl}: you need it at a precise moment, so it's under your thumb.
reasons.toggle:any: {fn} on {ctl}: you press it a few times a race.
reasons.rare:any: {fn} on {ctl}: you rarely need it, so it's on a control you have to reach for.
reasons.shared:f1_drs_pit: Pit limiter on the same button as DRS: F1 25 does this by default (pit limiter in the pit lane, DRS on track).
reasons.mfd:dpad: MFD on {ctl}: {game} uses the D-pad for its MFD pages, so the control that sends the D-pad suits it.
reasons.pair:funky: {fn} on {ctl}: turning the funky switch gives + and − without letting go of the wheel.
reasons.pair:rotary: {fn} on {ctl}: the rotary switch clicks + and − (set it to ENC mode if your wheel has modes).
reasons.pair:buttons_mirrored: {fn}: + on {a_ctl} and − on {b_ctl}, the same button on each side of the wheel.
reasons.ptt:f1_far: Talk to Pitwall on {ctl}: a plain button you can hold. Map it to UDP Action {n} in F1 25 so Pitwall sees it.
reasons.ptt:screen: {game} doesn't send button presses, so talk to Pitwall with the iPad's talk button or hold Space on a keyboard.
reasons.single:thumb: {fn} on {ctl}: you use it {freq}, so it's under your thumb.
reasons.single:near: {fn} on {ctl}: you use it {freq}, and this is the best free control left.
reasons.single:far: {fn} on {ctl}: you rarely need it, so it's on a control you have to reach for.
reasons.menu:control: {fn} on {ctl}: four directions on one control, as the game's menu expects.
reasons.kept: {fn} stays on {ctl}: you said you already have it there.
reasons.mfd_binding: {fn}: {game} changes it on its MFD pages, so it needs no button of its own.
reasons.single:thumb_rare: {fn} on {ctl}: you rarely need it, but this thumb button was free.
reasons.shared:same_button: {fn} on {ctl}: {game} uses the {other} button for it (unverified).
reasons.default:game: {fn} on {ctl}: {game}'s own default for this wheel, so there's nothing to change.

warnings.game_specific: {ctl} works only if {game} reads this wheel's extra buttons (unverified).
warnings.folded: {ctl} sends the same signal as another control, so the game can't tell them apart.
warnings.unknown: What {ctl} sends on {platform} isn't known: check it in the game.
warnings.mps_mode: Rotary switches step + and - only in ENC mode.
warnings.only_games: Community sources say only {games} reads this control (unverified).
warnings.unverified_row: Unverified in {game}: check the game's controls list for it.
warnings.unknown_push: What {ctl} sends when pushed in on {platform} isn't known: check it in the game.
